chunk_map.heading: Exercise: Take it to the team (H1 + lede)
Phase 1: Sketch the way of working
Phase 4: Find the bottleneck, draft both plans
Phase 6: Put Monday on the board and in the team folder

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L33 "Then name one thing the file needed that stayed on its sender's laptop" resolves to "the file" named L25; L77 "which assumptions" resolves to L73 "what would have to be true"; L87 "the first thing your wider team decides" resolves to team/what-goes-in.md in the same chunk; L67 "Monday's questions" and L91 "Stand at the frame" resolve to the Way of working frame named L17 and the Monday header of chunk 6. Harm (a projected slide pointing at nothing) absent; session artifacts (the call, the draft) are exercise carve-out.

Closest: L87 "On Day 1 it was the three of you deciding what your agents could read" and L9/L19 "Day 2". These name the training's own days and unpack the claim in the same sentence, not an opener by deck position; the cited artifacts team/what-goes-in.md and the Day 2 draft are named documents the student holds (navigational carve-out).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Resolved against the module set: team/five-users.md (apt101-five-users.md), team/chosen-bet.md (choose-the-bet), way-of-working.md (apt101-make-your-piece.md), team/what-goes-in.md (apt101-what-goes-in.md, send-it-off), agents/ instruction file (apt101-send-it-off.md). grep -ln over curriculum/exercises/apt101-*.md found each. Closest: L19 "the draft made on Day 2" (way-of-working.md exists in make-your-piece).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L27 guess-post-it precedes L29 run and L33 "line in the output that went generic". Reveal comes after the guess in reading order; setup sentences are verbed ("writes one sentence on a post-it: what you expect it to return"); no pronoun resolves only to the screen.
Smallest chunk is Phase 1 (L13-19), two paragraphs: the two post-its and the three columns. Each carries its own claim.

Closest: chunk 6 "Put Monday on the board and in the team folder" (L81-91): body covers the plans to the team folder, team/what-goes-in.md and the board read-back, so the header is true. Chunk 4 "Find the bottleneck, draft both plans" matches L58 verbatim.

Closest: L11 "They will decide whether agents join their work, and they already have a way of doing it" and L9 "your team does not want your agents, they want a job done": single contrast, no Not-X-Not-Y-Z chain. L64-65 and L19 lists carry concrete content per leg. grep '—' body count 0. No superlatives, no number+retraction, no abstraction-noun stack.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE of beat|surface|firing|compendium|forcing|mood|connections|leap|artefact|trace|judge over body L1-92 returned no hits (rc=1). Day, frame, call, shape are ordinary workshop words.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 3 (L43-46) four bold handles, each 2-3 words, the four sharing strategies as a scanned menu of options (bold marks the option name, check_student_facing section 34 verbatim); chunk 4 (L64-65) two role labels, each 3 words, handle cap met. No bolded sentences; chunks 0 and 2 carry one bold each ("The team lead drives", "The designer").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise is included standalone at curriculum/trainings/agentic-product-teams-101/learn-faster-than-the-market.md:39 ([Exercise: Take it to the team](exercises/...)), so it renders under .phase--exercise; all six Phase sections are ## chunks in the deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js -> "OK - 55 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." Phases 1-6 consecutive; L11 "all but Phase 2" resolves in-file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js curriculum/exercises/apt101-take-it-to-the-team.md -> "OK - 55 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." Closest: L17 "Everything else in the frame answers to those two" (a peer edit during this run replaced "Everything below them"; re-read and re-checked at the new sha); frame is the Miro board, not page geometry; no accept-note owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body carries no in-deck links (grep -c "](" over body = 0); the rule is a review surface and states there is no rule on links.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise headings are phase labels: "Phase 1: Sketch the way of working" ... "Phase 6: Put Monday on the board and in the team folder" (L13-81); H1 "Exercise: Take it to the team". No claim owed on a phase label.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: L91 "It is a proposal. The team that lives with it decides." and L79 "The old way stayed because it did the job well enough." Both carry an instruction-bearing reason (how to read the board; why not to blame the team), not a restated header or a koan, and the maintainer block names the proposal stance in Role in Day 3. No doctrine restatement or pedagogy commentary found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: git log -p on the file: the only ## changes are renumbering (Phase 2..5 to 3..6, inserted Phase 2) and 75ca30f5 "Test the switch, imagine it failed" to "Test the switch"; Phase 5 body (assumptions + failure story, L73-79) still answers the header. No retitled slide keeps old-job bullets.

notes: Cross-class (technical/behavior): chunk 3 body L41-46 lists four shapes (share context, skill, output, interface) while the apt101-d3-the-job-your-team-hires prompt asks for four different shapes (a file they run, a page they read, a habit in a meeting, a person who walks them through it); the body line L48 'pick the shapes' then does not match the prompt's menu. Not a slides rule.
